εὗρεν σοφίαν ἀγαθήν, εὗρεν χάριτας. Ὁ δὲ κατέχων μοιχαλίδα, ἄφρων καὶ ἀσεβής:
Ὁ δὲ κατέχων κακίαν, ἄφρων καὶ ἀσεβής. Πλοῦτος προστίθησι φίλους πολλούς:
Πλοῦτος γνώσεως καὶ σοφίας προστίθησιν ἡμῖν ἀγγέλους φίλους πολλούς· ὁ δὲ
ἀκάθαρτος ἀπὸ τοῦ δοθέντος αὐτῷ ἐκ παιδὸς ἀγγέλου χωρίζεται· ἡ γὰρ πνευματικὴ
φιλία ἐστὶν ἀρετὴ καὶ γνῶσις θεοῦ, δι' ὧν συναπτόμεθα πρὸς φιλίαν ταῖς ἁγίαις
ἀγγελικαῖς δυνάμεσιν, εἴγε οἱ μετανοοῦντες ἄνθρωποι χαρᾶς αἴτιοι γίνονται τοῖς
ἀγγέλοις. οὕτως καὶ ὁ σωτὴρ φίλους καλεῖ τοὺς δούλους ποτέ, τῆς μείζονος αὐτοὺς
θεωρίας καταξιώσας. οὕτω καὶ Ἀβραὰμ πλουτήσας ἐν γνώσει τὴν μυστικὴν ἐκείνην
παρατίθησι τράπεζαν τοῖς κατὰ τὴν μεσημβρίαν φίλοις φανεῖσιν αὐτῷ. Σαοὺλ δὲ καὶ
ἀπὸ τοῦ ὑπάρχοντος φίλου διὰ τὴν κακίαν χωρίζεται· γέγραπται γάρ· Καὶ ἀπέστη
πνεῦμα θεοῦ ἀπὸ Σαούλ, καὶ πνεῦμα πονηρὸν παρὰ κυρίου ἔπνιγεν τὸν Σαούλ·
πνεῦμα κυρίου λέγων τὸν ἄγγελον· Ὁ ποιῶν γάρ φησιν τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ
πνεύματα, καὶ τοὺς λειτουργοὺς αὐτοῦ πῦρ φλέγον. ὅτι δὲ καὶ ἄγγελοι τοὺς
ἀνθρώπους πεπίστευνται, διδάσκει ἐν τοῖς εὐαγγελίοις ὁ κύριος, Ὁρᾶτε, λέγων, μὴ
καταφρονήσητε ἑνὸς τῶν μικρῶν τούτων, ὅτι οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτῶν διὰ παντὸς βλέπουσι
τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς. καὶ πάλιν ὁ Ἰακώβ· Ὁ ἄγγελος ὁ
ῥυόμενός με ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν κακῶν. καὶ ὁ Ζαχαρίας· Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ ἄγγελος ὁ λαλῶν
ἐν ἐμοί. Ὁ δὲ ἐγκαλῶν ἀδίκως οὐ μὴ διαφύγῃ: Ὅσοι τοὺς περὶ κρίσεως καὶ προνοίας
ἀγνοοῦντες λόγους τὸν δημιουργὸν βλασφημοῦσιν, οὗτοι ἐγκαλοῦσιν ἀδίκως· καὶ
ὅσοι πάλιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἰδίων παθῶν ἐνοχλούμενοι νομίζουσιν ἀκατόρθωτον εἶναι τὴν
ἀρετήν, οὗτοι τῷ δεδωκότι τὸν νόμον ἐγκαλοῦσιν ἀδίκως. Ἔννοια ἀγαθὴ τοῖς
εἰδόσιν αὐτὴν ἐγγιεῖ: Τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ γνῶσιν νῦν ὠνόμασεν ἔννοιαν, καὶ τοὺς εἰδότας
αὐτὴν τοὺς καθαροὺς τῇ καρδίᾳ. Ὃς δὲ ἐρεθίζει λόγους οὐ σωθήσεται: Οἱ ἐμπαθεῖς
λογισμοὶ ἐρεθίζουσι τὴν ψυχὴν πρὸς κακίαν. Οὐ συμφέρει ἄφρονι τρυφή: Οὔτε ἡ
νοητὴ τρυφὴ οὔτε ἡ αἰσθητὴ συμφέρει τῷ ἄφρονι· τὴν μὲν γὰρ καταπατήσει τοῖς
ποσί, χοῖρος φιλήδονος ὤν· ὑπὸ δὲ τῆς αἰσθητῆς τρυφῆς ἡ σὰρξ αὐτοῦ κινηθήσεται.
Ἐλεήμων ἀνὴρ μακροθυμεῖ, τὸ δὲ καύχημα αὐτοῦ ἐπέρχεται παρανόμοις: Εἰ ὁ
καυχώμενος ὀρθῶς ἐν κυρίῳ καυχᾶται, ὁ δὲ κύριος ἡμῶν σοφία ἐστίν, ὁ καυχώμενος
ἄρα ὀρθῶς ἐν σοφίᾳ καυχᾶται· τὸ καύχημα 100 τοίνυν τοῦ μακροθύμου καὶ
ἐλεήμονος, ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἡ σοφία καὶ ἡ γνῶσις αὐτοῦ, ἐπέρχεται τοῖς παρανόμοις,
ἀπαλλάττον αὐτοὺς τῆς κακίας, νῦν μὲν ἐνδεχομένως, ἀναγκαίως δὲ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ
μέλλοντι. Βασιλέως ἀπειλὴ ὁμοία βρυγμῷ λέοντος: Ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν πῦρ μὲν
καταναλίσκον καὶ λέων ὀργιζόμενος γίνεται πρὸς τοὺς ἁμαρτάνοντας, κατακαίων
ξύλα χόρτον καλάμην, καὶ τὴν σάρκα τὴν στρατευομένην κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος
ἀναλίσκων· φῶς δὲ καὶ δρόσος πρὸς τοὺς κατορθοῦντας, δεικνὺς αὐτοῖς τῶν
γεγονότων τοὺς λόγους, καὶ κατασβεννύων τὰ πεπυρωμένα βέλη τοῦ πονηροῦ, καὶ
περιψύχων τὸν ἐκ τῆς πρακτικῆς συμβαίνοντα καύσωνα. Οὐχ ἁγναὶ εὐχαὶ ἀπὸ
μισθώματος ἑταίρας: Τὴν ἀκάθαρτον ψυχὴν ἑταίραν ὠνόμασεν· καὶ ταύτης τὸ
μίσθωμα τὴν κατάστασιν εἴρηκεν, ἀφ' ἧς οὐ καθαραὶ γίνονται προσευχαί. Οἶκον καὶ
ὕπαρξιν μεριοῦσι πατέρες: Τὸ μὲν διδάσκειν τοὺς υἱοὺς περὶ ἀρετῆς καὶ γνώσεως
θεοῦ, πατέρων ἐστίν· τὸ δὲ σοφίαν δοῦναι τοῖς παισί, τοῦ κυρίου ἐστίν· γυναῖκα γὰρ
ἐνταῦθα τὴν σοφίαν λέγει· Ἐράσθητι γάρ φησι τῆς σοφίας, καὶ τηρήσει σε· τίμησον
αὐτήν, ἵνα σε περιλάβῃ. Ὃς φυλάσσει ἐντολήν, τηρεῖ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν: Αἱ ἐντολαὶ
ὡς πρὸς μὲν τὸν ἐντειλάμενον θεὸν καλοῦνται ἐντολαί· ὡς δὲ πρὸς τὸν ὁδεύοντα
νοῦν ἐν αὐταῖς καλοῦνται ὁδοί· καὶ πάλιν ἐπειδὴ ἐπὶ μαρτύρων οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς
13
ἐδόθησαν αἱ ἐντολαί, λέγονται μαρτύρια· διὸ καὶ ὁ δεξάμενος αὐτὰ νοῦς ὀνομάζεται
μάρτυς, ὅστις ψευσάμενος αὐτὰ οὐκ ἀτιμώρητος ἔσται. Κατὰ δὲ τὸ δόμα αὐτοῦ
ἀνταποδώσει αὐτῷ: ∆όμα νῦν τὴν καθαρότητα τῆς καρδίας ὠνόμασεν· κατ'
ἀναλογίαν γὰρ τῆς ἀπαθείας ἡμῶν καταξιούμεθα γνώσεως. Κακόφρων ἀνὴρ πολλὰ
ζημιωθήσεται: Ἐγὼ νομίζω τὴν μὲν πολλὴν ζημίαν στέρησιν περιέχειν τῆς θεωρίας
τῶν γεγονότων, τὴν δὲ προσθήκην τῆς ψυχῆς ἀφανισμὸν τῶν φυσικῶν περὶ θεοῦ
ἐννοιῶν, παντάπασιν αὐτῆς εἰς ἀλογίαν περιπεσούσης. καὶ ὁ σωτὴρ δὲ ἐν τοῖς
εὐαγγελίοις φησίν· Τί ὠφεληθήσεται ἄνθρωπος, ἐὰν τὸν κόσμον ὅλον κερδήσῃ, τὴν
δὲ ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολέσῃ καὶ ζημιωθῇ; ἀλλ' ἐνταῦθα μὲν ἡ ἀπώλεια τὴν ἄγνοιαν
english: He found good wisdom; he found grace. But he who holds a net is a fool and impious; and he who holds onto wickedness is a fool and impious.

Wealth adds many friends: wealth of knowledge and wisdom adds to us many friendly angels; but the unclean one is separated from the angel given to him from childhood; for spiritual friendship is virtue and knowledge of God, through which we are joined to holy angelic friendships by divine powers, if repentant men become causes of joy to the angels. Thus also the Savior calls his servants friends at last, having deemed them worthy of the greater vision. Thus also Abraham, having become rich in that mystical knowledge, sets a table for the friends appearing to him at midday. But Saul is separated even from his existing friend because of wickedness; for it is written: 'And the Spirit of God departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord tormented Saul' (1 Sam 16:14); 'a spirit of the Lord' saying the angel: 'For he says [the Maker] makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a flaming fire' (Ps 104:4). Since also angels watch over men, the Lord teaches in the Gospels: 'See,' saying, 'do not despise one of these little ones, for their angels always see the face of my Father in heaven' (Matt 18:10). And again Jacob: 'The angel who delivers me from all evils' (Gen 48:16). And Zechariah: 'And the angel was speaking in me' (Luke 1:19). But he who accuses unjustly shall not escape: Those who, being ignorant of the words concerning judgment and providence, blaspheme the Creator, these accuse unjustly; and again, those who, being troubled by their own passions, think virtue to be impossible, these accuse Him who gave the law unjustly.

A good concept draws near to those who know it: He now named the knowledge of God 'concept,' and those who know it, the pure in heart. But he who provokes [the words] shall not be saved: Passionate thoughts provoke the soul toward wickedness. Luxury does not benefit a fool: Neither intellectual luxury nor sensual luxury benefits the fool; for he will trample the former with his feet, being a lover of pigs; and by the sensual luxury, his flesh will be moved. A merciful man is patient, but his boast comes to nothing...

If one boasts rightly in the Lord, and our Lord is wisdom, then the one boasting thus boasts rightly in wisdom. The boasting of the long-suffering and merciful—which is his wisdom and his knowledge—comes upon the lawless, freeing them from wickedness, now somewhat and necessarily in the age to come.

The threat of a king is like a lion's roar: Our Lord becomes a consuming fire and an angry lion toward those sinning, burning wood, brush, and reed, and consuming the flesh that wages war against the spirit; but toward those walking uprightly, he is light and dew, showing them the words of things that have happened, and quenching the inflamed arrows of the evil one, and refreshing the heat arising from the practical life.
Not pure thanks from a prostitute's reward: He named the unclean soul a prostitute; and regarding this, he called the reward the condition, from which they do not become pure prayers.

Fathers divide house and substance: To teach the sons about virtue and the knowledge of God is the work of fathers; but to give wisdom to the children is the work of the Lord; for there he calls wisdom a wife: For he says, 'She loved wisdom, and she will keep you; honor her, so that she may take hold of you.'

He who keeps a commandment keeps his own soul: The commandments are called commandments as toward the God who commands; but as toward the mind walking in them, they are called ways; and again, because the commandments were given upon the witnesses of heaven and earth (Heb 1:2), they are called testimonies; therefore also he who received them is named a witness, who, having not lied about them, will not be dishonored.
According to his gift he will repay him: He named now the purity of heart a gift; for by analogy of our apatheia, we are made worthy of knowledge.

A man of evil mind will suffer much loss: I think the great loss contains the deprivation of the contemplation of things that have happened, and the addition of the soul [is] the destruction of the natural notions concerning God, the whole of which falls into irrationality. And the Savior says in the Gospels: 'What will a man profit, if he gains the whole world and loses his soul and is harmed?' (Matt 16:26). But here the loss is ignorance.

σωμάτων καὶ ἀσωμάτων ἐμφαίνει· ἡ δὲ ζημία τὴν ἐσχάτην ἀλογίαν παρίστησιν. Ἵνα
σοφὸς γένῃ ἐπὶ γήρως: Μετὰ τὴν ὀρθὴν πολιτείαν ἐστὶν ἡ γνῶσις· τὸ γὰρ Ἐπ'
ἐσχάτων ἐνταῦθα οὐ τὸν χρόνον σημαίνει, ἀλλὰ τὴν μετὰ τὰς πρακτικὰς ἀρετὰς
καθαρότητα. Φόβος κυρίου εἰς ζωὴν ἀνδρί, ὁ δὲ πλανώμενος αὐλισθήσεται ἐν τόποις
οἷς οὐκ ἐπισκοπεῖται ὁ αἰώνιος: Εἰ φόβος κυρίου εἰς ζωὴν ἀνδρί, φόβος δὲ κυρίου
παιδεία καὶ σοφία, ζωὴ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς παιδεία ἐστὶν καὶ σοφία. ἀλλὰ Χριστὸς λέγει·
Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ζωή· ὁ Χριστὸς ἄρα ἐστὶν παιδεία καὶ σοφία. τὸ οὖν γνῶναι παιδείαν καὶ
σοφίαν γνῶναί ἐστιν τὸν Χριστόν· ὁ οὖν ἄφοβος ἔσται ἐν κακίᾳ καὶ ἀγνωσίᾳ, ἐν αἷς
οὐκ ἔστιν Χριστός.
101 Ὁ ἐγκρύπτων χεῖρας αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν κόλπον ἀδίκως, οὐδὲ τῷ στόματι
αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ προσαγάγῃ αὐτάς: Ο μὴ ὀρθῶς βιοὺς κρύπτει ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ αὐτοῦ τὰς
χεῖρας ἀδίκως, τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γῆν ἐργάσασθαι μὴ βουλόμενος μηδ' ἐμπλησθῆναι ἄρτων·
αἱ γὰρ πρακτικαὶ ἀρεταὶ χειρῶν ἐπέχουσι λόγον, τὸν ἄρτον τῷ στόματι ἡμῶν
προσφέρουσαι, τὸν ἀπὸ τῶν οὐρανῶν καταβάντα καὶ ζωὴν διδοῦντα τῷ κόσμῳ. Ὁ
ἀτιμάζων πατέρα καὶ ἀπωθούμενος μητέρα υἱὸς αἰσχυνθήσεται καὶ ἐπονείδιστος
ἔσται: ∆ιὰ τῆς παραβάσεως τοῦ νόμου τὸν θεὸν ἀτιμάζει, καὶ τὴν μητέρα δὲ
ἀπωθεῖται, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἡ παιδεία· εἴπερ ἀνὴρ δίκαιος γεννᾶται εἰς ζωήν, ἡ δὲ
δικαιοσύνη ἀπὸ πασῶν συνίσταται τῶν ἀρετῶν. Υἱὸς ἀπολειπόμενος φυλάξαι
παιδείαν πατρὸς μελετήσει ῥήσεις κακάς: Οἱ ἀκάθαρτοι λογισμοὶ ῥήσεις εἰσὶ κακαὶ ἐν
τῇ ψυχῇ γεννώμεναι τοῦ μὴ τετηρηκότος τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ ἐπουρανίου πατρός.
Ἀκόλαστον οἶνος καὶ ὑβριστικὸν μέθη: Εἰ θυμὸς δρακόντων ὁ οἶνος αὐτῶν,
ἀκόλαστον δὲ ὁ οἶνος, ἀκόλαστον ἄρα ὁ θυμός, ἀκολάστους τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ποιῶν,
καὶ ὑβριστικὸν ἡ ὀργή· αὕτη γὰρ ἡ μέθη ἀπὸ ζέοντος τοῦ θυμοῦ πέφυκε γίνεσθαι. εἰ
δὲ οἴνου ναζιραῖοι κατὰ τὸν νόμον ἀπέχονται, θυμοῦ ἄρα τοὺς ναζιραίους ἐκτὸς
εἶναι νενομοθέτηται. Οὐδὲν (LXX οὐ) διαφέρει ἀπειλὴ βασιλέως θυμοῦ λέοντος:
Ἐνταῦθα τὸν Χριστὸν ἄντικρυς εἴρηκε βασιλέα· ὁ γὰρ τοῦτον διὰ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν
παροξύνων ἁμαρτάνει εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν. Ὡσαύτως ὁ δανιζόμενος σῖτον ἐν
ἀμητῷ: Εἰ ἔστιν ἐν ἀμητῷ σῖτον δανείσασθαι, ἔστιν καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ μέλλοντι
νοητὸν σῖτον δανείσασθαι παρὰ τῶν ἐργασαμένων ἐν τοῖς ἓξ ἔτεσι τὴν ἑαυτῶν γῆν,
καὶ τρεφόντων ἐν τῷ ἑβδόμῳ ἔτει χήραν καὶ ὀρφανούς. Μακαρίους τοὺς παῖδας
αὐτοῦ καταλείψει: Οὓς κατ' ἀρετὴν δηλονότι γεγέννηκεν. Κακολογοῦντος πατέρα ἢ
μητέρα σβεσθήσεται λαμπτήρ: ∆ύναται ὁ αὐτὸς Χριστὸς κατ' ἐπίνοιαν καὶ πατὴρ
εἶναι καὶ μήτηρ· πατὴρ μὲν τῶν πνεῦμα ἐχόντων υἱοθεσίας, μήτηρ δὲ τῶν δεομένων
γάλακτος καὶ οὐ στερεᾶς τροφῆς· καὶ γὰρ ὁ ἐν Παύλῳ λαλῶν Χριστὸς πατὴρ μὲν τῶν
Ἐφεσίων ἐγίνετο, σοφίας αὐτοῖς ἀποκαλύπτων μυστήρια, μήτηρ δὲ Κορινθίων, γάλα
ποτίζων αὐτούς. Μερὶς ἐπισπουδαζομένη ἐν πρώτοις: Ἣ πρὸς καιρὸν λιπαίνει μερὶς
σὸν φάρυγγα, ὕστερον μέντοι πικρότερον χολῆς εὑρήσεις. Μὴ εἴπῃς· Τίσομαι τὸν
ἐχθρόν: Μὴ εἴπῃς καθ' ὑπερηφανίαν κινούμενος· Ἐγὼ μόνος τοῖς ἐχθροῖς 102
πολεμήσω, ἀλλ' ὑπόμεινον τὸν κύριον ἵνα σοι βοηθήσῃ. καὶ ὁ ∆αυὶδ φησίν· Οὐκ ἐπὶ
14
τῷ τόξῳ μου ἐλπιῶ, καὶ ἡ ῥομφαία μου οὐ σώσει με· καὶ πάλιν· Ψευδὴς ἵππος εἰς
σωτηρίαν· καὶ ἐὰν μὴ κύριος οἰκοδομήσῃ οἶκον καὶ φυλάξῃ πόλιν. Στάθμιον μέγα
καὶ μικρὸν καὶ μέτρα δισσά, βδελυκτὰ (LXX ἀκάθαρτα) ἐνώπιον κυρίου ἀμφότερα:
Τὸν παρά τισι θρασύδειλον λεγόμενον στάθμιον μέγα καὶ μικρὸν εἶναι νομίζω· καὶ
καθόλου πᾶσαν ὑπερβολὴν καὶ ἔλλειψιν στάθμιον μέγα καὶ μικρὸν εἶναι νομίζω·
ἑκάτερα γὰρ κακίαι. Μέτρα δισσά: Ὁ εὖ μὲν πάσχειν ὑφ' ἑτέρου βουλόμενος, αὐτὸς
δὲ ὁμοίως ἄλλους ἀναπαύειν μὴ προαιρούμενος, μέτρα ἔχει δισσά, μὴ πειθόμενος
τὴν ἐντολὴν τὴν λέγουσαν· Πάντα ὅσα θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, πάντα
english: It manifests things of bodies and things incorporeal; and the loss demonstrates the ultimate irrationality. So that one becomes wise in old age: After right conduct comes knowledge; for the 'end things' here does not signify time, but purity after the practical virtues.

The fear of the Lord is unto life for a man (Proverbs 14:27), but the wanderer will stumble in places where the age is not observed. The fear of the Lord is unto life for a man, and the fear of the Lord is discipline and wisdom; the life of the man is discipline and wisdom. But Christ says: 'I am the life' (John 14:6); therefore Christ is discipline and wisdom. To know, then, discipline and wisdom is to know Christ; so the one without fear will be in evil and ignorance, in which Christ is not.

He who hides his hands in his bosom unjustly, nor with his mouth will he ever bring them forth: He who does not rightly, hides the hands unjustly in his soul, not wishing to work his own land nor to be filled with bread; for the practical virtues have a logic, bringing the bread to our mouths, the one descended from the heavens and giving life to the world.

He who dishonors a father and pushes away a mother will be ashamed and will be a reprobate: Through the transgression of the law he dishonors God, and he pushes away the mother, who is the discipline; if a righteous man is born unto life, and righteousness consists of all the virtues. A son left to fail in keeping the discipline of a father will meditate bad sayings: The impure thoughts are bad sayings being born in the soul of one who has not kept the commandments of the heavenly Father.

Unrestrained wine and insolent drunkenness: If their wine is the wrath of dragons, and the wine is unrestrained, then the wrath is unrestrained, making men unrestrained, and the anger is insolent; for this drunkenness is accustomed to come from a boiling wrath. If, however, Nazirites abstain from wine according to the law, then the Nazirites are outside of wrath...

It is established as law. Neither the threat of a king nor the fury of a lion differs (LXX: not). Here Christ is spoken of as a king in opposition; for he, provoked by sins, sins against his own soul.

Likewise, the one lending grain in a year of famine: If it is possible to borrow grain in a year of famine, it is also possible to borrow spiritual grain in the age to come from those who worked their own land in the six years and fed the widow and the orphan in the seventh year. He will leave his children blessed: those whom he has brought forth according to virtue.

A father or mother being slandered, a lamp will be extinguished: The same Christ is able, in thought, to be both father and mother; father to those possessing the spirits of adoption, but mother to those needing milk and not solid food; for the Christ speaking in Paul became a father to the Ephesians, revealing mysteries of wisdom to them, but a mother to the Corinthians, giving them milk to drink.

A part being studied in the first [stages]: It may for a time moisten your throat with part, but later you will find it more bitter with bile. Do not say: I will strike the enemy: Do not say this, moved by pride: I alone will fight the enemies, but endure the Lord so that he may help you. And David says: I trust not in my bow, and my sword shall not save me (Psalm 118:24-25); and again: A false horse toward salvation (Proverbs 14:31); and if the Lord builds not a house, and keeps not a city (Psalm 127:1).

A great and small weight and double measures, both are an abomination (LXX: unclean) before the Lord (Proverbs 20:10): I think that what is called a great and small weight by some is considered reckless; and I think that a great and small weight is any total excess or deficiency; for both are evils. Double measures: He who intends to suffer well from another, but does not pre-meditate to similarly refresh others, has double measures, not obeying the commandment which says: All that you want men to do to you, all [so do you to them] (Matthew 7:12).

καὶ ὑμεῖς ὁμοίως ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς. Οὖς ἀκούει καὶ ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς ὁρᾷ: Οὐχ ὁ κακῶς ὁρῶν
ὀφθαλμὸς ἔργον ἐστὶν τοῦ κυρίου, ἀλλ' ὁ ὁρῶν· καὶ οὐ τὸ κακῶς ἀκοῦον οὖς ἔργον
ἐστὶν τοῦ κυρίου, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἀκοῦον. καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἄλλων δὲ μελῶν τοῦ σώματος
ὡσαύτως λεκτέον· χρήσῃ δὲ τῷ ῥητῷ τούτῳ πρὸς τοὺς κατηγοροῦντας ἡμῶν τοῦτο
τὸ σῶμα καὶ τὸν δημιουργὸν ἐνυβρίζοντας. ∆ιάνοιξον δὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς σου καὶ
ἐμπλήσθητι ἄρτων: ∆ιὰ μὲν τῶν ἀρετῶν ἀνοίγομεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τῆς ψυχῆς, διὰ
δὲ τῆς σοφίας νοητῶν πληρούμεθα ἄρτων. Θνητὸς δὲ πῶς ἂν ἐννοήσαι (LXX νοήσαι)
τὰς ὁδοὺς ἑαυτοῦ: Οὐ δύναται νοῆσαι τὰς ὁδοὺς κυρίου ὁ ἔτι θνητὸς καὶ μὴ
συναποθανὼν τῷ Χριστῷ.
Παγὶς ἀνδρὶ ταχύ τι τῶν ἰδίων ἁγιάσαι: Ἡ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς μετάνοια οὐ
δικαίοις συμβαίνει ἀλλὰ ἀδίκοις· ἄδικοι δὲ μηδὲν ἀπερισκέπτως ὑπισχνείσθωσαν τῷ
θεῷ· μετὰ γὰρ τὸ εὔξασθαι μετανοεῖν γίνεται. Καὶ ζυγὸς δόλιος οὐ καλὸν ἐνώπιον
αὐτοῦ: Ζυγὸν δόλιον λέγει τὸν νοῦν πεφυκότα μὲν δικαίως κρίνειν τὰ πράγματα,
παρακλίνοντα δὲ τῇ τοῦ ἀντεξουσίου ῥοπῇ. Λικμήτωρ ἀσεβῶν βασιλεὺς σοφός:
Χωρίζειν (ζων?) τὰ ἄχυρα ἀπὸ τοῦ σίτου. Καὶ ἐπιβαλεῖ αὐτοῖς τροχόν: Ποίησον
αὐτοὺς ὡς τροχόν. 103 Φῶς κυρίου πνοὴ ἀνθρώπων: Εἰ τὸ φῶς τοῦ κυρίου ἡ γνῶσις
τοῦ κυρίου ἐστίν, τὸ δὲ φῶς τοῦ κυρίου ἡ πνοὴ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐστίν, ἡ ἄρα γνῶσις
τοῦ κυρίου ἡ πνοὴ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐστίν. τὸν δὲ ἐν ἀγνοίᾳ διάβολον φαίνειν
δοκοῦντα λύχνον ὠνόμασεν, ἐκκενοῦντα τὸν νοῦν τῶν ἀγαθῶν καὶ
μετασχηματιζόμενον εἰς ἄγγελον φωτός. Ποιεῖν δίκαια καὶ ἀληθεύειν ἀρεστὸν παρὰ
κυρίου μᾶλλον ἢ θυσιῶν αἷμα: Ἐκβάλλει τὸ ῥητὸν τοῦτο τὴν διὰ τῶν ἀλόγων ζώων
θυσίαν· θυσία γὰρ τῷ θεῷ πνεῦμα συντετριμμένον. Ἁγνὰ δὲ καὶ ὀρθὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ:
Εἰ ἁγνὰ καὶ ὀρθὰ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἓν δὲ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ ἐστὶν καὶ ὁ νοῦς, ὀρθὸς
ἄρα καὶ ἁγνὸς ἐκτίσθη παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου ὁ νοῦς. Κρεῖσσον οἰκεῖν ἐπὶ γωνίας ὑπαίθρου
ἢ ἐν κεκονιαμένοις μετὰ ἀηδείας (LXX ἀδικίας) καὶ ἐν οἴκω κοινῷ: Τῷ οἴκῳ τῷ
κεκονιαμένῳ καὶ κοινῷ τὴν ὕπαιθρον γωνίαν ἀντέθηκεν· εἰ δὲ ὁ οἶκος ὁ
κεκονιαμένος καὶ κοινὸς ἡ κακία ἐστίν, ἡ ὕπαιθρος γωνία ἡ ἀρετή ἐστιν· γωνία
τοίνυν ὕπαιθρός ἐστιν πρᾶξις θεωρίας ἐφαπτομένη καὶ φωτιζομένη ὑπὸ τοῦ τῆς
δικαιοσύνης ἡλίου. καλῶς δὲ καὶ ὁ Παῦλος τὸν ἀρχιερέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων τοῖχον εἶπεν
κεκονιαμένον, τυπτηθησόμενον ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ· καὶ ὁ σωτὴρ δὲ ἐν τοῖς εὐαγγελίοις
τοὺς Φαρισαίους τάφους εἶπεν κεκονιαμένους. εὖ δὲ καὶ τὸ Ἐπὶ γωνίας εἶπεν, ἔνθα ὁ
λίθος κεῖται ὁ ἀποδοκιμασθεὶς ὑπὸ τῶν οἰκοδόμων καὶ γενόμενος κεφαλὴ γωνίας·
κοινὸν δὲ εἶπεν ὃ μὴ τοῦ ἑνός ἐστιν θεοῦ. ∆όσις λάθριος ἀνατρέπει ὀργάς: ∆όσις
λάθριός ἐστιν, ἵν' ὃ ποιῇ ἡ δεξιὰ μὴ γινώσκῃ ἡ ἀριστερά. Ἀνὴρ πλανώμενος ἐξ ὁδοῦ
δικαιοσύνης ἐν συναγωγῇ γιγάντων ἀναπαύσεται: Ἡ συναγωγὴ τῶν γιγάντων ἡ
κακία καὶ ἡ ἀγνωσία ἐστίν. Κρεῖσσον οἰκεῖν ἐν γῇ ἐρήμῳ ἢ μετὰ γυναικὸς θυμώδους
καὶ μαχίμης: Καὶ ὁ ∆αυὶδ φησίν· Ἐν γῇ ἐρήμῳ καὶ ἀβάτῳ καὶ ἀνύδρῳ, οὕτως ἐν τῷ
ἁγίῳ ὤφθην σοι. ἔρημος τοίνυν γῆ ἐστὶν ἡ ἀρετὴ ἡ μὴ ἔχουσα τοὺς παλαιοὺς
ἀνθρώπους οἰκοῦντας τοὺς φθειρομένους κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ἀπάτης· διὸ οὐδὲ
εὑρίσκει ἐν αὐτῇ ἀνάπαυσιν ὁ διάβολος, εἴγε διέρχεται δι' ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητῶν
15
ἀνάπαυσιν καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκει· αὐτὸς γὰρ βασιλεύς ἐστι πάντων τῶν ἐν τοῖς ὕδασι. καὶ
πάλιν τῆς σοφίας Στεγναί φησιν αἱ διατριβαὶ οἵκων αὐτῆς (27,31). εἰ δὲ τοῦτο,
οὐκοῦν καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἡ μάχιμος καὶ γλωσσώδης καὶ ὀργίλος ἡ κακία ἐστίν, ἥτις τὸν
συζῶντα αὐτῇ ποιεῖ μάχιμον καὶ γλωσσώδη καὶ ὄργιλον. 104 Θησαυρὸς ἐπιθυμητὸς
ἀναπαύσεται ἐπὶ στόματος σοφοῦ: Σοφία κυρίου ἀναπαύσεται ἐν καρδίᾳ σοφοῦ·
ἄφρονες δὲ ἄνδρες διαφθεροῦσιν αὐτήν. Πόλεις ὀχυρὰς ἐπέβη σοφός: Σοφία ἐστὶν
πόλις ὀχυρά, ἐν ᾗ οἱ σοφοὶ κατοικοῦσιν, λογισμοὺς καθαιροῦντες καὶ πᾶν ὕψωμα
ἐπαιρόμενον κατὰ τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Ὃς φυλάσσει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν
γλῶσσαν, διατηρεῖ ἐκ θλίψεως τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ: Στόμα καὶ γλῶσσαν, ψυχὴν καὶ
νοῦν· ψυχὴν δέ φασιν θυμὸν καὶ ἐπιθυμίαν, ὅπερ τινὲς παθητικὸν μέρος ὀνομάζουσι
τῆς ψυχῆς. Ἀσεβὴς ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἐπιθυμεῖ ἐπιθυμίας κακάς: Ἀγγέλων μὲν τὸ μὴ
ἐπιθυμεῖν ποτὲ ἐπιθυμίας κακάς· ἀνθρώπων δὲ τὸ ποτὲ μὲν ἐπιθυμεῖν, ποτὲ δὲ μὴ
ἐπιθυμεῖν ἐπιθυμίας κακάς· δαιμόνων δὲ τὸ ἀεὶ ἐπιθυμεῖν ἐπιθυμίας κακάς. τὸ γὰρ
Ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν τὸ διὰ βίου δηλοῖ. τοιοῦτόν ἐστιν καὶ τὸ Ἐν φόβῳ κυρίου ἴσθι
ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν, ἀντὶ τοῦ διὰ βίου. Ἵππος ἑτοιμάζεται εἰς ἡμέραν πολέμου: Ἵππον
english: And you also do the same to them. An ear hears and an eye sees: It is not the eye seeing badly that is the work of the Lord, but the seeing; and it is not the ear hearing badly that is the work of the Lord, but the hearing. And the same must be said concerning the other members of the body. Use this saying against those who accuse us of this body and who insult the Creator.

Open your eyes and be filled with bread: Through virtues we open the eyes of the soul, and through the wisdom of intelligible things we are filled with bread. And how can a mortal understand (LXX: know) his own ways: A mortal cannot understand the ways of the Lord if he has not yet died together with Christ.

A wise man is a swift snare to ungodly men: Repentance toward good things does not happen to the righteous but to the unrighteous; yet the unrighteous did not expect anything from God without consideration; for after praying, repentance occurs. And a deceitful yoke is not good before Him: The mind, which is naturally disposed to judge things rightly, is called a deceitful yoke when it swerves by the inclination of the will.

A wise man is a winnower of an ungodly king: Separating the chaff from the sieve. And he sets a wheel upon them: Make them as a wheel. The light of the Lord is the breath of men: If the light of the Lord is the knowledge of the Lord, and the light of the Lord is the breath of men, then the knowledge of the Lord is the breath of men. He named the devil, who seems to be in ignorance, a lamp, emptying the mind of good things and transforming himself into an angel of light.

To do justice and to speak truth is more pleasing to the Lord than the blood of sacrifices: This saying casts out the sacrifice through irrational animals; for a sacrifice to God is a crushed spirit. But His works are pure and right: If the works of God are pure and right, and one of His works is the mind, then the mind was created pure and right by the Lord.

It is better to dwell in a corner of the open air than in dusty places with iniquity (LXX: injustice) and in a common house: He set the open-air corner against the dusty and common house; but if the dusty and common house is evil, the open-air corner is virtue; therefore, an open-air corner is a practice of contemplation, touching and being illuminated by the sun of righteousness.

Paul has spoken well of the high priest of the Jews as a wall having been plastered, to be struck by God; and the Savior in the gospels has spoken of the Pharisees as tombs having been plastered. Also well did he speak of the stone at the corner, where the stone lies which was rejected by the builders and having become a head of the corner; and he has spoken commonly of that which is not of the one God.

A secret gift subverts passions: a gift is secret, so that what the right hand does the left hand may not know. A man wandering from the way of righteousness will rest in a gathering of giants: the gathering of giants is malice and ignorance.

It is better to dwell in a desert land than with a woman angry and contentious: and David says, 'In a desert land and uncultivated and waterless, so I appeared to you in holiness' (Psalm 107:4-5). A desert land is therefore the virtue which does not have the old men dwelling in it, those decaying according to the desires of deception; therefore the devil does not even find rest in it, if he passes through waterless places seeking rest and does not find it; for he himself is king of all those in the waters. And again regarding wisdom, he says the habits of its houses are sighs. If this is so, is not also the woman who is contentious and talkative and angry malice, which makes the one living with her contentious and talkative and angry.

A desirable treasure will rest upon the mouth of a wise man: The wisdom of the Lord will rest in the heart of a wise man (Proverbs 15:13, 15:33); but foolish men destroy it. A wise man ascended fortified cities: Wisdom is a fortified city, in which the wise dwell, pulling down reasonings and every exaltation being lifted up against the knowledge of Christ (2 Corinthians 10:5). He who guards his mouth and his tongue preserves his soul from tribulation: Mouth and tongue, soul and mind; for they say soul, [meaning] spirit and desire, which some call a passive part of the soul.

An impious man all the day desires evil desires: For angels, never to desire evil desires; for men, sometimes to desire and sometimes not to desire evil desires; but for demons, always to desire evil desires. For 'all the day' signifies through life. Such is also 'be in the fear of the Lord all the day' (Proverbs 23:17), instead of 'through life.' A horse is prepared for a day of war (Proverbs 21:31): A horse...

λέγει τὸν νοῦν. Ἐπιβήσῃ γάρ φησιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἵππους σου, καὶ ἡ ἱππασία σου σωτηρία.
καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Παύλου ὁ κύριος Τοῦ βαστάσαι τὸ ὄνομά μου φησίν. Αἱρετώτερον ὄνομα
καλὸν ἢ πλοῦτος πολύ (edd. πολύς): Τὴν σημαινομένην ἀρετὴν ὑπὸ τοῦ οἰκείου
ὀνόματος ὄνομα εἶπεν καλόν· τοῦτο γὰρ τὸ ὄνομα καλόν ἐστιν, ὅπερ ἔχει τὸ
σημαινόμενον ἀγαθόν. οὕτως οὐδὲ τὴν ἄδικον γυναῖκα δικαιοσύνην καλουμένην
ἐπαινέσομεν, ἀλλὰ τὴν ἔχουσαν τὴν δικαιοσύνην, κἂν ἀδικία ὀνομάζηται. Πλούσιος
καὶ πτωχὸς συνήντησαν ἀλλήλοις, ἀμφοτέρους δὲ ἐποίησεν ὁ κύριος (edd. ὁ κύρ.
ἐποί.): Ὁ μὲν πλούσιος διὰ τῶν ἐλεημοσυνῶν καθαίρει θυμόν, κτώμενος τὴν
ἀγάπην· ὁ δὲ πένης διὰ τῆς πενίας ταπεινοφρονεῖν ἐκδιδάσκεται. Γενεὰ σοφίας,
φόβος κυρίου: Αὗται αἱ γενέσεις Νῶε· αὗται αἱ γενέσεις Ἀβραάμ. Τρίβολοι καὶ
παγίδες ἐν ὁδοῖς σκολιαῖς: Καὶ ὁ κύριος τῷ Ἀδὰμ φησίν· Ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους
ἀνατελεῖ σοι ἡ γῆ, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ἡ ψυχή. ἀκάνθας δὲ καὶ τριβόλους λέγει τὰς ἁμαρτίας,
ἀφ' ὧν καὶ ὁ στέφανος ἐπλάκη τοῦ Χριστοῦ· αὐτὸς γὰρ ἦρεν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ
κόσμου. Πλούσιοι πτωχῶν ἄρξουσιν: Ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ μέλλοντι οἱ ἐν παντὶ
πλουτισθέντες, ἐν πάσῃ γνώσει καὶ 105 πάσῃ σοφίᾳ, ἄρξουσι τῶν ἀκαθάρτων καὶ
ἐστερημένων τούτου τοῦ πλούτου. τίνες δὲ οἱ οἰκέται καὶ τίνες οἱ δεσπόται, νῦν οὐκ
ἀναγκαῖον δημοσιεύειν, διὰ τὸ εἶναι τὸν περὶ αὐτῶν λόγον μυστικὸν καὶ βαθύτερον.
Ματαιότητα δὲ ἔργων αὐτοῦ συντελέσει: Τὴν ματαιότητα τῶν ἔργων διὰ τῆς ἀρετῆς
ὁ κύριος καὶ τῆς γνώσεως συντελεῖ. Νίκην καὶ τιμὴν περιποιεῖται ὁ τὰ (edd. om.)
δῶρα διδούς: ∆ῶρα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τὰς ἀρετὰς ὀνομάζει, δι' ὧν νικῶν τὸν διάβολον
τίμιον ἑαυτὸν παρέχει τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἀφαιρεῖται τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχὴν ἀπὸ τῶν
κτησαμένων, αὐτὴν δαιμόνων. Ἔκβαλε λοιμὸν ἐκ συνεδρίας (edd. ἐκ συνεδρίου
λοιμ.), καὶ συνεξελεύσεται αὐτῷ νεῖκος: Τὴν χειρίστην κατάστασιν συνέδριον εἶπεν,
ἀφ' ἧς ὁ σοφὸς Σολομὼν ἐκβάλλεσθαι τὸν ἄνθρωπον βούλεται διὰ πνευματικῆς
διδασκαλίας· τὸ δὲ νεῖκος τὴν φιλονεικίαν σημαίνει. δύναται δὲ λοιμὸν καὶ τὸν
διάβολον λέγειν, ὃν δεῖ ἀποδιώκειν τῆς ψυχῆς· ἐὰν γὰρ καθίσῃ ἐν αὐτῇ, διὰ τῆς
ἀκαθαρσίας πάντας τοὺς ὀρθοὺς λογισμοὺς ἀτιμάζει. συνέδριον δὲ καὶ ὁ ἀπόστολος
τὴν ψυχὴν ἀποδείκνυσι, δι' ὧν κατηγοροῦντας λογισμοὺς εἰσάγει καὶ
ἀπολογουμένους· Μεταξὺ γάρ φησιν ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ
ἀπολογουμένων. ὅπου δὲ κατηγορία καὶ ἀπολογία, ἐκεῖ καὶ συνέδριον. Χείλεσι
ποιμαίνει βασιλεύς: Ὁ διατηρῶν τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν κύριος, αὐτὸς καὶ διὰ τῆς
πνευματικῆς γνώσεως ποιμαίνει ἡμᾶς, ἥντινα γνῶσιν φαυλίζει ὁ παραβαίνων τὸν
νόμον αὐτοῦ. σημειωτέον δὲ ὅτι βασιλεὺς ὢν ὁ Χριστὸς λέγεται διὰ τῆς
16
συγκαταβάσεως ποιμαίνειν ἡμᾶς· Ἐγὼ γάρ φησιν εἰμὶ ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός. εἰ δὲ
βασιλεὺς μέν ἐστι βασιλευόντων, ποιμὴν δὲ προβάτων, ἔσται ποτὲ μόνον βασιλεὺς
τῶν προβάτων εἰς τὸ βασιλικὸν μεταβάντων ἀξίωμα. Προφασίζεται καὶ λέγει
ὀκνηρός· Λέων ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς: Ὁ ἐχθρὸς ἡμῶν διάβολος ὡς λέων περιέρχεται ζητῶν
τίνα καταπίῃ· ὅντινα φοβούμενος ὁ ὀκνηρὸς πρὸς τὴν ἐργασίαν τῶν ἀρετῶν
ἀναδύεται. Ὁ δὲ μισηθεὶς ὑπὸ κυρίου ἐμπεσεῖται εἰς αὐτόν: Ὁ Ἰὼβ οὐ μισηθεὶς ὑπὸ
κυρίου ἀλλὰ δοκιμῆς ἕνεκεν ἐμπέπτωκεν εἰς αὐτόν. Ῥάβδος δὲ καὶ παιδεία μακρὰν
ἀπ' αὐτοῦ: Μακρὰν ἀπὸ τῆς καρδίας τοῦ ἄφρονός ἐστιν ἡ ῥάβδος ἡ ἐκ τῆς ῥίζης
Ἰεσσαί. 106 Ὁ συκοφαντῶν πτωχὸν (edd. πένητα) πολλὰ ποιεῖ τὰ ἑαυτοῦ κακά:
Ὥσπερ ὁ διάβολος συκοφαντεῖ ἡμᾶς λαμβάνων παρ' ἡμῶν τὰς ἀρετὰς ἃς μὴ δέδωκεν
ἡμῖν, οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς συκοφαντοῦμεν αὐτὸν λαμβάνοντες παρ' αὐτοῦ τὰς κακίας ἃς
μὴ δεδώκαμεν αὐτῷ. καὶ καθὸ μὲν λαμβάνομεν παρ' αὐτοῦ τὰς κακίας, ὡς παρὰ
πένητος ἐν ἀρεταῖς λαμβάνομεν· καθὸ δὲ τὰς ἀρετὰς ἡμῶν διδόαμεν αὐτῷ ἐπ'
ἐλαττώσει ἡμῶν, ὡς πλουσίῳ ἐν κακίᾳ διδόαμεν. ἔλεγεν δέ τις τῶν γερόντων, ὅτι
ἡμεῖς ἐσμὲν οἱ συκοφάνται οἱ Χριστὸν συκοφαντοῦντες, πτωχεύσαντα δι' ἡμᾶς καὶ
μηδὲν ὀφείλοντα ἡμῖν, καὶ λαμβάνοντες παρ' αὐτοῦ πολλὰ καὶ διδόντες τῷ σατανᾷ
ἐπὶ ταπεινώσει τῶν ἡμετέρων ψυχῶν. Παράβαλε σὸν οὖς λόγοις σοφῶν: Οὗτος
ἀκούει τῶν τοῦ θεοῦ λόγων, ὁ ποιῶν τὰ προστασσόμενα ὑπ' αὐτῶν· οὐ γὰρ οἱ
ἀκροαταὶ νόμου δίκαιοι παρὰ θεῷ, ἀλλ' οἱ ποιηταὶ τοῦ νόμου δικαιωθήσονται. Καὶ
σὺ δὲ ἀπόγραψαι αὐτὰ σεαυτῷ τρισσῶς ἐν βουλῇ καὶ γνώσει (edd. εἰς βουλὴν κ.
γνῶσιν) ἐπὶ τὸ πλάτος τῆς καρδίας σου: Ὁ πλατύνας διὰ τῆς καθαρότητος τὴν
english: He says, 'the mind shall mount upon your horses, and your cavalry shall be salvation.' And regarding Paul, the Lord says, 'to bear my name.'

A name more excellent than much wealth: He said that the virtue signified by the proper name is beautiful; for this is the beautiful name, which possesses the signified good. In this way, we shall not praise an unjust woman even if she is called justice, but rather the one possessing justice, even if she is named injustice.

A rich man and a poor man met one another, and the Lord made both of them [equal]. The one rich man purifies his passion through almsgiving, cultivating love; the one poor man is trained to be humble through his poverty.

The generation of wisdom is the fear of the Lord: These are the generations of Noah; these are the generations of Abraham. Snares and pits in crooked paths: And the Lord says to Adam, 'the earth shall bring up thorns and snares for you' (Genesis 3:18), that is, the soul. But he says thorns and snares [mean] sins, from which even the crown of Christ was struck; for he himself took away the sin of the world (John 1:29).

The rich shall rule over the poor (Proverbs 22:7): In the age to come, those having been enriched in every way, in all knowledge and all wisdom, shall rule over the unclean and the deprived of this wealth. And who are the servants and who are the masters, it is not necessary to publish now, because the word concerning them is mystical and deeper.

But the futility of his works shall complete: The Lord completes the futility of works through virtue and knowledge. He acquires victory and honor, he who gives gifts: He calls the virtues the gifts of man, through which, conquering the devil, he presents himself as precious to God, and his own soul is snatched away from those who have possessed it, from the demons.

Cast out a plague from the council, and strife shall come out with him: He called the governing state a council, from which the wise Solomon wishes to cast out man through spiritual teaching; and the strife signifies contention. But he may also mean the plague as the devil, whom it is necessary to drive away from the soul; for if he sits within it, through impurity he dishonors all the righteous thoughts.

The apostle also shows the soul as a tribunal, through which accusing thoughts are brought in and defending thoughts are brought in; for he says that thoughts are accusing or defending one another. Where there is accusation and defense, there is a tribunal.

A king shepherds with a rod: The Lord, who preserves our souls, himself shepherds us through spiritual knowledge, which knowledge the one transgressing his law despises. It should be noted that Christ, being a king, is said to shepherd us through condescension; for he says, 'I am the good shepherd' (John 10:11). But if he is a king over kings and a shepherd of sheep, he will at some time be only a king, the dignity of one having passed over into the royal.

The sluggard is faced with a lion in the paths: Our enemy the devil prowls like a lion seeking someone to swallow up (1 Peter 5:8), whom the sluggard, fearing, avoids in the work of virtues. He who is hated by the Lord will fall into him: Job did not fall into him because he was hated by the Lord, but because of testing.

A rod and instruction are far from him: The rod from the root of Jesse is far from the heart of the foolish (Isaiah 11:1). The slanderer does many evils of his own to the poor: Just as the devil slanders us, taking from us the virtues which he did not give to us, so also we slander him, taking from him the evils which we did not give to him. And just as we take the evils from him as if from a poor man in virtues, so also we give our virtues to him to our own diminishment, as if we were giving to a rich man in evil. One of the elders used to say that we are the slanderers, slandering Christ, who became poor because of us and owed nothing to us, yet we take much from him and give to Satan to the debasement of our souls.

Compare yourself with wise words: This one hears the words of God, the one doing the things protected by them; for the hearers of the law are not righteous before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified (James 1:22). καρδίαν αὐτοῦ νοήσει τοὺς τοῦ θεοῦ λόγους, τούς τε πρακτικοὺς καὶ τοὺς φυσικοὺς
καὶ τοὺς θεολογικούς· πᾶσα γὰρ ἡ κατὰ τὴν γραφὴν πραγματεία τέμνεται τριχῶς, εἰς
ἠθικὴν καὶ φυσικὴν καὶ θεολογικήν· καὶ ἀκολουθεῖ τῇ μὲν πρώτῃ αἱ παροιμίαι, τῇ δὲ
δευτέρᾳ ὁ ἐκκλησιαστής, τῇ δὲ τρίτῃ τὰ ἄσματα τῶν ἀσμάτων. Μὴ δίδου σεαυτὸν εἰς
ἐγγύην, αἰσχυνόμενος πρόσωπον: Οἱ τοὺς φαύλους ἀναδεχόμενοι λογισμοὺς καὶ
τούτῳ τιμῶντες τὸν πονηρὸν σπουδαζέτωσαν ὅση δύναμις διὰ τῶν ἀγαθῶν
λογισμῶν ἀποδιδόναι τοὺς χείρονας· ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ ἰσχύσωσι τοῦτο ποιῆσαι, λήψονται
τὸ στρῶμα τὸ ὑπὸ τὰς πλευρὰς τῆς ψυχῆς, τοῦτ' ἔστι τὴν ἀρετήν· αὕτη γὰρ τοῦ μὲν
ἑστῶτος ἐν τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ νοῦ ἱμάτιον λέγεται, τοῦ δὲ λοιπὸν πεσόντος διὰ τῶν
φαύλων λογισμῶν ὑπόστρωμα καλεῖται. Μὴ μέταιρε ὅρια αἰώνια, ἃ ἔθεντο οἱ
πατέρες σου: Ὁ μετατιθεὶς τὰ ὅρια τῆς θεοσεβείας δεισιδαιμονίαν ἢ ἀσέβειαν αὐτὴν
ἀποδείκνυσι· καὶ ὁ μετατιθεὶς τὰ ὅρια τῆς ἀνδρείας θρασύτητα ἢ δειλίαν αὐτὴν
ἀπεργάζεται. ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἀρετῶν καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν δογμάτων καὶ ἐπ'
αὐτῆς τῆς πίστεως· νοητέον· μάλιστα δὲ τοῦτο τηρητέον ἐπὶ τῆς ἁγίας τριάδος· ὁ γὰρ
μὴ θεολογῶν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον διαλύει τὸ βάπτισμα· ὁ δὲ καὶ ἄλλους τινὰς
ὀνομάζων θεοὺς δῆμον εἰσάγει θεῶν. Εἰ δὲ ἀπληστότερος εἶ, μὴ ἐπιθύμει τῶν
ἐδεσμάτων αὐτοῦ: Οὐ γὰρ πάντες χωροῦσι τὴν μυστικωτέραν διάνοιαν τῆς γραφῆς.
107 Ταῦτα γὰρ ἔχεται ζωῆς ψευδοῦς: ∆εῖ τὴν θείαν γραφὴν νοητῶς νοεῖσθαι καὶ
πνευματικῶς· ἡ γὰρ κατὰ τὴν ἱστορίαν αἰσθητὴ γνῶσις οὐκ ἔστιν ἀληθής. Μὴ
συνδείπνει ἀνδρὶ βασκάνῳ: Εἰ ὁ βάσκανος σῖτα ἀσεβείας ἐσθίει καὶ οἴνῳ παρανόμῳ
μεθύσκεται, οὐ δεῖ δὲ συνδείπνειν τούτῳ, οὐ χρὴ ἄρα εἶναι ἀσεβῆ καὶ παράνομον·
αὗται γὰρ αἱ κακίαι λυμαίνονται γνῶσιν πνευματικήν. Εἰς ὦτα ἄφρονος μηθὲν (edd.
μηδὲν) λέγε: Μηθὲν λέγε συνετόν, τοῦτ' ἔστιν βαθὺ καὶ μυστικόν· οὐ δεῖ γὰρ βάλλειν
τὰς μαργαρίτας ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων. Εἰς δὲ κτῆμα ὀρφανῶν μὴ εἰσέλθῃς: Κτῆμα
ὀρφανῶν ἡ κακία ἐστίν, δι' ἣν ἐστερήθησαν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς σωτῆρος. Ἀλλ' ἢ ἐν
φόβῳ κυρίου ἴσθι ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν: Εἰ τῷ φόβῳ κυρίου ἐκκλίνει πᾶς ἀπὸ κακοῦ,
καλῶς παραινεῖ διὰ παντὸς τοῦ βίου ἐκκλίνειν ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ παντὸς κακοῦ. Ἐὰν γὰρ
17
τηρήσῃς ταῦτα (edd. αὐτά), ἔσται σοι ἔγγονα (ut cod. Alex.): Τοὺς ὀρθοὺς λογισμοὺς
καὶ τὰ πνευματικὰ θεωρήματα ἔγγονα εἶπεν τοῦ νοῦ· διὸ καὶ ἄτεκνός ἐστιν ψυχὴ ἡ
μὴ ἔχουσα ταῦτα τὰ ἔγγονα, ἅπερ πέφυκε τίκτεσθαι ἀπὸ τοῦ πνευματικοῦ νυμφίου.
Καὶ ῥακώδη ἐνδύσεται πᾶς ὑπνώδης: Οὐκ ἔστιν ἔνδυμα γάμου διερρηγμένον ἱμάτιον
καὶ ῥακῶδες. Καὶ μὴ καταφρόνει ὅτι γεγήρακεν ἡ μήτηρ σου: Ἤκουσά τινος τῶν
γερόντων τὴν ψυχὴν εἰπόντος μητέρα τοῦ νοῦ· αὕτη γάρ φησιν διὰ τῶν πρακτικῶν
ἀρετῶν εἰς φῶς προάγει τὸν νοῦν· ψυχὴν δὲ ἔλεγεν τὸ παθητικὸν μέρος τῆς ψυχῆς,
ὅπερ διαιρεῖται εἰς θυμὸν καὶ ἐπιθυμίαν· διὰ γὰρ ἀνδρείας, φησίν, καὶ σωφροσύνης
κτώμεθα σοφίαν καὶ γνῶσιν θεοῦ· ἀνδρεία δὲ καὶ σωφροσύνη θυμοῦ καὶ ἐπιθυμίας
εἰσὶν ἀρεταί. Μὴ μεθύσκεσθε οἴνῳ: Οἱ οἶνοι οὗτοι ἐκ τῆς Σοδομιτικῆς εἰσὶν ἀμπέλου.
108 Μὴ ὁμιλεῖτε ἀνθρώποις, καὶ ὁμιλεῖτε ἐν περιπάτοις: Νοῦς ὁμιλῶν ἐν περιπάτοις
ἀξίως περιπατεῖ τῆς κλήσεως ἧς ἐκλήθη. Ἐὰν γὰρ εἰς τὰς φιάλας καὶ τὰ ποτήρια δῷς
τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς σου: Ἡ μὲν κατὰ διάνοιαν ἁμαρτία ἔοικε φιάλῃ, ἡ δὲ κατ' ἐνέργειαν
ποτηρίῳ. Ὕστερον περιπατήσεις γυμνότερος ὑπέρου: Πολλὰ κρούει τὸ ὕπερον καὶ
οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸν τόπον ὃν κρούει. τοῖς δὲ μαθηταῖς ὁ κύριος φησίν· Κρούετε, καὶ
ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν. Οἱ ὀφθαλμοί σου ὅταν ἴδωσιν ἀλλοτρίαν, τὸ στόμα σου τότε
λαλήσει σκολιά: Νοῦς δεξάμενος ἀλλότριον νόημα μελετήσει λογισμοὺς κακούς· ὁ
δὲ τηρήσας ἑαυτὸν κληρονομήσει ζωήν. Καὶ ὥσπερ κυβερνήτης ἐν πολλῷ κλύδωνι:
Παντὶ ἀνέμῳ τῆς διδασκαλίας περιφερόμενος. Πότε ὄρθρος ἔσται: Ὄρθρος ψυχῆς
ἐστὶν ἐπίγνωσις ἁμαρτίας. Μετὰ κυβερνήσεως γίνεται πόλεμος: Οἱ περὶ τὴν πίστιν
ναυαγοῦντες οὐ μετὰ κυβερνήσεως πολεμοῦσιν τοῖς πνεύμασι τοῖς ἀντικειμένοις τῇ
θεολογίᾳ. δυνατὸν δὲ καὶ ἐπὶ πάσης ἀρετῆς τὸ αὐτὸ τοῦτο εἰπεῖν· ἔστιν γὰρ καὶ περὶ
σωφροσύνην ναυάγιον καὶ περὶ ἀγάπην καὶ περὶ ἀφιλαργυρίαν, καὶ περὶ ἕκαστον δὲ
δόγμα ὁμοίως τῆς καθολικῆς καὶ ἀποστολικῆς ἐκκλησίας συμβαίνει ναυάγιον. εἰ δὲ
μετὰ κυβερνήσεως πολεμεῖν δεῖ τοῖς ἀντικειμένοις, ναυμαχίᾳ παραπλήσιος ἡμῶν
ἐστὶν ὁ βίος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Ἐν πύλαις σοφοὶ οὐκ ἐκκλίνουσιν ἐκ στόματος (edd. add.
english: His heart will perceive the words of God, both the practical, the natural, and the theological. For every matter according to the Scripture is divided into three parts: ethical, natural, and theological; and the proverbs follow the first, the Preacher the second, and the songs of the senseless the third.

Do not give yourself as a guarantee, being ashamed of your face. Those who welcome evil thoughts and honor the wicked should strive for how much power through good thoughts can restore the bad; for if they are not able to do this, they will receive the layer under the sides of the soul, which is virtue; for this is called the garment of the mind standing in righteousness, but for the one having fallen through evil thoughts, it is called a cushion. Do not shift eternal boundaries, which your fathers set. He who shifts the boundaries of godliness demonstrates either superstition or impiety; and he who shifts the boundaries of courage achieves either audacity or cowardice. Likewise also concerning the other virtues and concerning the dogmas and concerning faith itself: it must be perceived; but above all this must be kept concerning the Holy Trinity; for he who does not theologize divides the Holy Spirit by baptism; and he who names others as gods brings the multitude into gods. And if you are more unlearned, do not desire his bonds: for not all contain the more mystical intellect of the Scripture. For these things have the life of falsehood: it is necessary that the divine Scripture be perceived intellectually and spiritually; for the sensory knowledge according to history is not true.

Do not join a man with a basket. If the basket eats the wheat of impiety and drinks lawless wine, one must not join with it; therefore it is not right to be impious and lawless; for these vices defile spiritual knowledge. Say nothing to the ears of a fool: say nothing sensible, that is, deep and mystical; for it is not necessary to cast pearls before swine (Matt 7:6). Do not enter into the property of orphans: wickedness is the property of orphans, through which they were deprived of the Savior in the heavens. But rather be in the fear of the Lord all the day (Ps 112:1): if everyone turns away from evil through the fear of the Lord, it advises well to turn us away from...

from all evil. For if you keep these things, you will have offspring (cf. Alex. cod.): 'The righteous thoughts and the spiritual contemplations are offspring,' he said to the mind; therefore also a soul is barren which does not have these offspring, which it is nature to bring forth from the spiritual bride. And everyone who is sleepy will dress in rags: There is no wedding garment torn and in rags. And do not despise that your mother has become old: I heard one of the elders saying the soul is the mother of the mind; for this [mother] he says leads the mind into light through the practical virtues; but he called the passive part of the soul 'the soul', which is divided into spirit and desire; for through courage, he says, and temperance, we acquire wisdom and knowledge of God; and courage and temperance are virtues of spirit and desire.

Do not get drunk with wine: These wines are from the vine of Sodom. Do not talk with men, but talk in walks: A mind talking in walks walks worthily of the calling wherewith it was called. For if you give your eyes to the bowls and the cups: Sin according to intellect resembles a bowl, but according to energy a cup. Later you will walk more nakedly than the proud: The proud person knocks much and does not open the place which he knocks at. But to the disciples the Lord says: Knock, and it shall be opened to you (Matt 7:7). Your eyes, when they see something foreign, then your mouth will speak crookedly: A mind having received a foreign thought will meditate on evil logismoi; but the one having kept himself will inherit life.

And like a pilot in much swell: Being tossed about by every wind of teaching. When will it be dawn?: The dawn of the soul is the knowledge of sin. After guidance comes war: Those shipwrecking regarding the faith do not fight with the spirits opposing theology after guidance; but it is possible to say this same thing regarding every virtue; for there is also shipwreck regarding temperance and regarding love and regarding freedom from greed, and regarding every dogma similarly a shipwreck happens to the catholic and apostolic church. And if it is necessary to fight with the opponents after guidance, life on the earth is near us like a naval battle. In gates the wise do not turn away from the mouth (Prov 31:23).

english: Of the Lord: The gates of the wise are the practical virtues, through which the wisdom of God enters. But impurity will be inflicted upon a man of misfortune: If virtue diminishes evil, and virtue makes evil manifest, this will happen in the age to come until evil ceases; for it has been set [to be said] that 'will be inflicted' instead of 'will be corrupted'; and impurity is corrupted either by practical [virtue] or by the punishment of severity. 'Save those being led to death and being killed without mercy, do not spare' (Psalm 85:13). Use this word for those being granted knowledge and those being negligent of the teaching, many of whom are being led by evil into death.

'Eat honey, my son, for it is a good thing, so that your throat may be sweetened' (Proverbs 24:13). He who is being benefited from the divine writings eats honey; but he who casts out the words from the things themselves, from which even the holy prophets and apostles have received, chews wax; and to eat honey is possible for everyone who wishes, but the wax is for the pure alone.

'Do not bring near the impious [thinking] you are just': Do not betray God for the sake of pleasure; for this one is thought to be just, and he will by no means abandon you. 'If your enemy falls, do not rejoice': For God turns his wrath away from the fallen one, having had mercy on him; but he is angry with the one who has been puffed up over the fall of his enemy; for everyone who rejoices is like the devil, who does not want all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. It should be noted, however, that he spoke of a man here as the enemy, for whom the Lord has enjoined us to pray in the Gospels (Matthew 5:44).

'For they will not bear children of the wicked': Evil [things] will not produce virtues and right doctrines, for these are the offspring of the soul, because they do not fear the Lord; but those being in the fear of the Lord will have offspring all day long, and their hope will not depart. english: Regarding his words: For it is not possible to add to the law of the Lord, nor is it possible to take away from it. 'Make me to have long false words and long pseudonymous knowledge.' Lest, having been filled with falsehood, I become so and say, 'Who sees me?' Lest—he says—having been filled, a listener becomes arrogant, and I say, 'No one shall know my own wisdom'; lest, having been filled with unapproachable knowledge, I appear to men as a liar, saying such things as those provided with blood and flesh are not able to know.

And the seventh [proverb] is also well-placed: 'Lest, being in need, I steal and swear by the name of God' (Matt 5:35); for someone steals foreign theories in order to fill a starving mind. But this happened before the arrival of the Savior; but now Paul says: 'Let him who stole steal no longer, but rather let him work righteousness, so that having acquired knowledge he may give to the one in need' (Eph 4:28); for what and what is it that is not ours, that we should steal, we who have believed in Christ? (1 Cor 6:7). For all things are ours, but we are Christ's, through whom all things came to be, and Christ is God's.

Or being in need, I will steal and swear by the name of my God: This one steals knowledge, not he who takes that of the predecessor, but he who subtracts from pseudonymous knowledge. For all those who have believed in Christ, receiving theories from the holy prophets and apostles, are not called thieves of foreign theories, but rather heirs of the patrimonial goods.

Do not deliver a servant into the hands of a master: To a fleeing mind, do not again deliver it to evil, if indeed everyone doing sin is a slave of sin; and sin is now called the devil, who works sin. But upon them shall come a good blessing: The good blessing is the intelligible blessing, which is distinguished from the sensible blessing.

Prepare your works for the exodus and prepare for the field: Our Lord in the Gospels named the world a field, but Solomon now has spoken of the field as the theory of the world; but the one in the Gospels, the field, is that of the composition of a human soul and body, for it is sensible; whereas the one indicated here, the field, is of the mind alone, being intelligible and composed from the words of this world, into which hearts enter.

Pure things. And you will not build your house: for a house is built with wisdom; but wisdom will not enter into a soul that is ill-skilled. And the walls of its stones are being undermined: apathy of a rational soul, established from the practical [virtues], is a wall.

Mocking the eye of a father and dishonoring the aged mother, crows cut him out of the ravines (Proverbs 30:17): these crows mystically nourish the righteous, but they slaughter the unrighteous, gouging out the eyes of injustice, because they mocked the Father and God of all, and dishonored the ancient knowledge that begot them; and regarding the crows that gouge out the eyes of the impious, he called them [ravens], but regarding those devouring him entirely, he named them eagles, because they believe in a partial purification for the former, and a total purification for the latter.
And a goat is considered a scapegoat: if the unpurified are standing as rivals on the left side of the Savior, the goat leads these; lest the goat now signifies the devil.

And the weak will not be able to judge rightly: they will not be able to teach rightly (Proverbs 31:9). Give drink to those in sorrows (Proverbs 31:9): he who is intoxicated by the potency of the master's house forgets his pains. And distinguish between the poor and the weak: poor means one lacking in knowledge, and weak means the unpurified.

The glory of God hides a word (Psalm 103:37): he who possesses the glory of God, he called the glory of God, and he who possesses the glory of the heavenly King, he named the glory of a king; for these hide the word of God within themselves, so that they might not sin, and they honor the commands through which they perform them. Often we have noted this, that those possessing virtues and evils are named by the virtues and the evils; thus, 'The Lord is just and loved justice,' instead of 'the just'; and 'The fear of the Lord hates injustice, insolence, and pride,' that is, the unjust, the insolent, and the proud. And here again he named the one possessing the glory of God and the one possessing the glory of the king, the glory of God and the glory of a king. ἀναιδὲς γλῶσσαν ἐρεθίζει: Τὸν διάβολον εἶπεν πρόσωπον ἀναιδές, ἐρεθίζοντα τὴν

Οὕτως γνῶσις θεοῦ ἐκ γῆς πραέων. Οὕτως ἄκοσμον δίκαιον πεπτωκέναι ἐναντίον
ἀσεβοῦς: Τῶν νοημάτων τοῦ νοῦ τὰ μὲν πτώματα αὐτοῦ λέγεται, τὰ δὲ ἐγέρσεις, τὰ

ὀνομάζεται· καὶ ἄλλα σκληρὰ καὶ μαλακά, καὶ εὐώδη καὶ δυσώδη, καὶ γλυκέα καὶ
πικρά, καὶ λεῖα καὶ ὀρθὰ καὶ σκολιά· καὶ πάλιν τὰ μὲν αὐτοῦ καλεῖται ἄκανθαι καὶ
english: He who honors the king honors his commands; for he who dishonors him, through the transgression of the law, dishonors him. Cast away the impious from the presence of a king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.

By the spiritual word, having killed the old man, the one decaying according to the desires of deception, he establishes his own mind in righteousness, which is said to be the throne of God; for nowhere else has wisdom, knowledge, and righteousness been permitted to sit, except in the rational nature; and all these are Christ. Nor does he stand in the places of the powerful.

Do not say, 'Above the stars I will set my throne, I shall be like the Most High' (Ps 113:4), for it is better to be spoken of regarding you by Zeus, and God exalted him, and granted him a name above every name (Acts 17:29). Do not fall headlong into battle too quickly: through battle he struck the evil. Whenever your friend reproaches you, withdraw to the rear, do not despise: and the Savior in the Gospels reproaches the cities in which most of his powers have become, because they did not repent: 'Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida!' (Matt 11:21). Grace and friendship set free, which you have kept for yourself, so that you may not become reproachable.

Solomon more densely remembers friend and friendship; therefore it is good now to attend to the name, what friendship intends to signify: for he says, 'Grace and friendship set free.' And yet the Savior in the Gospels says to the Jews who had believed in him: 'If you remain in my word, truly you are my disciples, and the truth will set you free' (John 8:31-32). And Paul again writes: 'Christ has freed us from the curse of the law' (Gal 3:13). If therefore friendship sets free, and the truth sets free, and the Savior sets free, Christ is the truth and the friendship; whence also all those having the knowledge of Christ are friends of one another.

Thus also the Savior has called the disciples friends, and John was a friend of the Bridegroom, and Moses and all the saints; and by this only friendship are his friends and friends of one another. But guard your paths with good sociality: the one having been taught concerning virtues and acting according to them guards his paths with good sociality.

A golden apple in a sardius setting: Just as a golden apple fits a sardius, so knowledge of God fits a pure soul. Before a golden and sardius setting, much wealth is laid out; a wise word for obedient ears: Cast a precious sardius before a golden setting, and the wisdom of the Lord into an impassive mind. Just as the departure of snow in a drought benefits against a heat: Just as snow cools a heatwave, so the knowledge of saints dissolves the toil of the soul.

And a soft tongue crushes bones: Now he named the irascible soul soft, which crushes the bones that were endowed to speak; Lord, who is like you? Bring a small amount with your foot to your friend: It is necessary to approach theological matters sparingly and not to do this densely, lest we say something of the unsaid things concerning God, and as impious ones fall away from knowledge, the mind being continuously unable to contemplate through its own weakness by such a theory. The way of evil and the path of lawlessness shall perish in an evil day: This is, that evil and lawlessness shall perish in the day of judgment.

Thus a fallen passion grieves the heart in the body: The passions falling upon the heart are evils; of which, by deprivation, the impassive one is named. Thus the sorrow of a man harms the heart: Sorrow is a choice, a deprivation of corrupt pleasure; but sorrow is praiseworthy, a deprivation of virtues and knowledge of God. For having done this, you will heap coals of fire upon his head: Through kindness and goodwill, purifying his ruling principle. But a shameless face provokes the tongue: He said the devil is a shameless face, provoking the soul; and everywhere Solomon says the tongue [is] the mind; therefore, this is not good to feel shame of the face in judgment.

Good news from afar from the earth: Thus knowledge of God from the earth is good. Thus the unseemly has fallen against the impious: Regarding the thoughts of the mind, its falls are called so, and its uprisings, and its descent, and its standing, and others a walk and some of its obstacles are named; and others hard and soft, and fragrant and malodorous, and sweet and bitter, and smooth and straight and crooked; and again some of its things are called thorns and...

english: Opposites are used: light and darkness, life and death, sickness and health; and again, falsehood and truth are named; and many other names the Scripture assigns according to the soul and its thoughts. As for what it assigns to the soul, to say but a few of many, these are: mind, soul, heart, man, man (male), woman, slave, servant, father, son, spirit, eye, mouth, lips, tongue, larynx, belly, womb, arm, finger, wood, nostril, sheep, ram, shepherd, and there are many more names of the soul, which cannot now be set forth due to the kind of commentaries that do not permit long-windedness.

Here, then, a righteous mind falls before Satan, having received an impure thought or a false dogma. And David says: 'All who descend to the earth shall fall before him' (Psalm 140:5). But this fall contains true knowledge and pure thoughts. Thus, a man who does nothing by design: 'Will' here means the inclination of the heart toward the better. 'A whip for the horse, a goad for the ox, and a rod for the fool' (Proverbs 26:3). The rod is now a symbol of punishment. He who sends a word through a foolish messenger makes a dream out of his own feet: 'Do not give holy things to dogs, nor cast pearls before swine' (Matthew 7:6). Removing the path of the legs and the proverb from the mouth of fools: 'Remove the evil path of the fool, and make a long distance of false knowledge from him.' He who releases a stone from a sling is like one giving glory to a fool: 'Knowledge does not suit a fool, and a stone is worthless in a golden sling' (Proverbs 26:11).

Much is frozen in the flesh of fools, for their ecstasy is crushed: If the ecstasy of fools, by which they were beside themselves of God, is crushed, they become pure again and approach God; for all flesh shall see the salvation of God (Luke 18:42). One must note here that he names the thickened souls from the evil flesh of fools; so also the Lord says: 'My Spirit shall not remain in these men, because they are flesh' (Psalm 51:11). Just as a dog, when it falls upon its own vomit and becomes loathsome, so a fool, turning away by his own wickedness...
Having cast his wickedness and turned again to it, he is like a dog eating his own vomit (Proverbs 26:11). A lazy man, having hidden his hand in his bosom, is unable to bring it forward.

If a tree of life is nourished from the fruits of righteousness, everyone who hides righteousness with unrighteousness will not eat from this tree. Just as one who holds a dog's muzzle, so is the one presiding over an alien judgment. Use this saying for those deciding certain unworthy ones in the sanctuary or by lot. Where there is no wrath, a battle will be stilled: He said, 'The wrathful man is a hothead' (Proverbs 25:20/14:30).

Smooth lips cover a wicked heart (Proverbs 14:30): Sorrow will not seize a pure heart, for it has driven away corrupt desires from it. If the enemy entreats you with a loud voice, do not be persuaded by him: Satan sometimes entreats us, tickling us through impure thoughts and spreading himself over us with the smoothness of pleasure, and sometimes he puts forth a voice so loud as if having been defeated, as if one should not be persuaded by one having unmitigated war against us.

For there are seven evils in his heart: These evils oppose the seven spirits. A soul being in abundance plays with masters, but a soul in want finds even bitter things sweet: A pure soul enjoys knowledge; but an impure soul considers false knowledge to be true knowledge.

Thus a man is enslaved when he is made a stranger from his own places: The place of the heart is virtue and knowledge, from which, having been made a stranger, a man falls into wickedness and ignorance and becomes a slave; because everyone who does sin is a slave of sin (John 8:34). A heart delights in myrrh, wine, and incenses: An impassive mind delights in manifold wisdom; but a passionate mind falls into ignorances.

Do not abandon your friend and your brotherly friend (Proverbs 17:17): They abandoned me, the fountain of living water (Jeremiah 2:13), and they dug pits for themselves. If you do not enter into your brother's house in misfortune: Such was the one who entered the wedding feasts and did not have wedding clothes (Matthew 22:11). A near friend is better than a brother living far away (Proverbs 18:24): Better is the one joined to me through true knowledge than the one joined to me through untrue knowledge. ἀρετῆς ἐπ' ἀρετὴν ἢ ἀπὸ γνώσεως ἐπὶ γνῶσιν ὑγιῶς μεταβαίνουσιν, τῆς ἀνθρωπίνης

ἐπὶ πλήθει 118 τοσούτῳ ὁδεύοντι ἀπὸ κακίας εἰς ἀρετήν. διὸ καὶ μόνη ἡ γνῶσις τῶν
ἁγίων ἀγγέλων τρέφει τὰς ἐν ἡμῖν ἀρετάς, ἀφ' ὧν ἐνδύεται σπλάγχνα οἰκτιρμοῦ
ψυχή, χρηστότητα, μακροθυμίαν, ταπεινοφροσύνην, πίστιν, ἐγκράτειαν, ἀγάπην, καὶ
τὰ ἐκ ταύτης γεννώμενα ἀγαθά. ὅτι δὲ πεδία καὶ ὁ ∆αυὶδ λέγει τὰς λογικὰς ψυχάς,

πάλιν μετ' ὀλίγα· Καὶ αἱ κοιλάδες πληθυνοῦσι σῖτον· κεκράξονται, καὶ γὰρ
ὑμνήσουσιν. ὕμνος δὲ καὶ κραυγὴ μόνη πέφυκεν ἐπισυμβαίνειν τῇ φύσει τῇ λογικῇ.
Ἀνὴρ ἐν ἀσεβείαις συκοφαντεῖ πτωχούς: Εἰ ἔστιν ἀνδρεῖος ἐν ἀσεβείαις, ἔστιν
ἀνδρεῖος καὶ ἐν ἀρεταῖς· καὶ εἰ ὁ ἀνδρεῖος ἐν ἀσεβείαις συκοφαντεῖ πτωχούς, ὁ
ἀνδρεῖος ἐν ἀρεταῖς παρακαλεῖ πτωχούς· οὐκοῦν πᾶς ὁ παρακαλῶν πτωχοὺς
ἀνδρεῖός ἐστιν ἐν εὐσεβείαις. Οἱ δὲ ἀγαπῶντες τὸν νόμον περιβάλλουσιν ἑαυτοῖς

κτᾶται καὶ γνῶσιν θεοῦ· εἰ δὲ οἱ ἀγαπῶντες τὸν νόμον περιβάλλουσιν ἑαυτοῖς
τεῖχος, νῦν τὸ τεῖχος τὴν ἀπάθειαν σημαίνει καὶ τὴν γνῶσιν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἅπερ μόνα

γὰρ ψυχῆς ἐστίν, λογισμοὶ ἐμπαθεῖς διὰ τοῦ σώματος ἐκτελούμενοι· ἀσωτία δὲ νοῦ

νόμου, καὶ αὐτὸς τὴν προσευχὴν αὐτοῦ ἐβδέλυκται: Οὐχ ὁ νόμος βδελύσσεταί τινος
english: Regarding what is said in the Gospel, 'even from him who does not have, that which he seems to have will be taken away' (Matt 25:29). This signifies, in my opinion, the intellectual remnants of virtues and the knowledge of God, which are taken from men who have used them badly.

'He who plants a fig tree shall eat its fruits' (Prov 24:13): Our Lord is the fig tree, for its fruit heals leprosy. 'If one dishonors a fool in the midst of a sitting, you will not take away his foolishness from him' (Prov 26:4-5): Not dishonoring the fool will not remove him from foolishness, but rather teaching him what kind of dishonor foolishness becomes to a stranger.

'Knowingly shepherd your souls' (Heb 13:17): Attend to yourself and direct your virtues, for men do not always remain equally strong in them; nor do they transition healthily from virtue to virtue or from knowledge to knowledge, [those] not easily receiving the human condition...; for he says 'generations' regarding virtues and knowledges, according to which the saints are born, and he shows this through what he writes: 'A generation of wisdom: the fear of the Lord, and riches, and glory, and life' (Prov 24:13-14).

This proverb should also be used toward the shepherds of the churches, to whom it is necessary to attend not to faces but to hearts, and to shepherd the sheep intellectually. 'Tend the green things in the field and shear the wool' (Song of Sol 2:16/4:16): He calls the mind a field, and the green things are the virtues existing within it by potentiality; the one tending them shears the wool, which is a symbol of the knowledge of God, which he also again calls a mountain pasture; for a mountain pasture is the knowledge of the holy powers, fitting the more irrational state of souls. It is the custom of Scripture to call the saints 'mountains.' Thus also David lifts his soul up to the mountains, whence his help shall come (Ps 121:1); and again, 'the mountains like rams, and the bulls like lambs of the flock, for the salvation of Israel' (Ps 98:7); for if angels rejoice over one repentant person, how much more over a multitude traveling from evil toward virtue. Therefore also...

Only the knowledge of the holy angels nourishes the virtues within us, from which the soul's organs of compassion are clothed: kindness, patience, humility, faith, self-control, love, and the good things born from these. For since the fields are also [metaphorical], and David speaks of rational souls, it is to be learned from here. For they say, 'Your fields shall indeed be filled with plenty' (Psalm 65:13); and again shortly after, 'And the barns shall be full of corn' (Psalm 65:14); they shall cry out, for they shall indeed sing (Psalm 96:11). For hymn and cry alone are suited to belong to rational nature.

A man who slanders the poor in impieties: If he is brave in impieties, he is brave also in virtues; and if the brave man slanders the poor in impieties, the brave man in virtues exhorts the poor; surely everyone who exhorts the poor is brave in pieties. But those who love the law surround themselves with a wall: Everyone who loves the law practices the law, and everyone who practices the law acquires apathy and knowledge of God; if then those who love the law surround themselves with a wall, now the wall signifies apathy and the knowledge of God, which alone is suited to guard the rational nature.

He who shepherds profligacy dishonors his father: He calls the mind a shepherd, and the passions within it are sheep, which he nourishes within himself through the transgression of the law, thereby dishonoring God; for profligacy is a sickness of the soul, consisting of passionate thoughts carried out through the body; but profligacy of the mind is the assumption of false dogmas and theories.

He who increases his wealth through usury and abundance brings it to the one who shows mercy to the poor: If the wealth of the impious is wickedness, and wise men will destroy it, it is evident that the righteous and wise are destroying wickedness by leading the impure toward virtue through spiritual teaching. He who turns his ear not to hear the law, he himself has detested his prayer: It is not the law that is detested by anyone.

english: Prayer, but God is the one who gave the law. And Paul says: 'The Scripture foretells what is to come' (Rom 5:2), instead of 'The one who gave the Scripture.' He who explains and reproves will be loved. I said: I will confess my lawlessness to the Lord, and you have forgiven the impiety of my heart.

A lion hungry and a wolf thirsty, who tyrannizes being a poor man of a meager nation: If those who hunger and thirst for righteousness are blessed (Matt 5:6), those who hunger and thirst for injustice are lions and wolves. A king in need is a great slanderer: The approaches of the evil king are evils and false doctrines; for those ruled by him approach these things to him.

A man who guarantees a murderer will be a fugitive and not in safety: He who guarantees Satan guarantees injustice, promising to him that he will render the fruits of injustice. And concerning this the Gospel also says as one defiled through murder and sedition was cast into prison (Acts 25:11). A lawless nation shall by no means obey: The lawless nation is the order of the demons, to which the educated son does not obey.

He who works his own land will be filled with bread: He who cleanses himself will be filled with knowledge, but the unclean will be filled with ignorance. He who is ashamed of the faces of the unrighteous is not good: If the virtues are the faces of the righteous, he is not good who is not ashamed of the virtues; and if evils are the faces of sinners, he is good who is not ashamed of the evils. An insolent man hastens to be rich: Therefore the merciful in the age to come, having been shown mercy by God and having become angels, shall rule over the ungodly. Such is the status and...

He promised his disciples that the Lord would give them to sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. A throne is that in which the mind sits, a spiritual knowledge, gathering together those who have wandered from godliness. And to judge there means to teach, as 'Open your mouth with the word of God and judge all things healthily' (Ps 89:8), instead of 'Teach.' It is also necessary to know this: that the merciful one, having grasped the staff, himself will not become a staff, but will rather make the staff merciful.

And in the destruction of those, the righteous will be multiplied: If the ungodly perish in being ungodly, they will become righteous; for destruction now means the removal of ungodliness. Thus also Matthew, the tax collector (Matt 9:9), having been lost, the Lord granted him righteousness. For when it is burning, there is no healing (Matt 13:12): He did not say that once the flame has ceased there is no healing, but that while it is burning there is no healing, as one still having clearly wood, hay, or straw (Matt 13:12); if even for those being burned, health is found to approach after the ember.

And when ungodly rulers prevail, men groan: All those who are under the rulers and the authorities and the cosmic rulers of this darkness (Eph 6:12), all these groan. He who pastures prostitutes, destroys wealth: He who nurtures wickedness destroys wealth.

—Otherwise. A shepherd is a good mind having acquired passionless thoughts; and a shepherd is an evil mind having acquired passionate thoughts. If this is so, then surely a passionate thought is a goat, and a passionless thought is a sheep; therefore also the Lord stands the goats on the left and the sheep on the right (Matt 25:32-33); and he calls them both goats and sheep...

λογικῆς ὀνομάζει. Ὃς μερίζεται κλέπτῃ, μισεῖ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν: Ὁ κλέπτης, φησίν,
οὐκ ἔρχεται εἰ μὴ ἵνα κλέψῃ καὶ θύσῃ καὶ ἀπολέσῃ. Ἐὰν δὲ ὅρκου προτεθέντος
ἀκούσαντες μὴ ἀναγγείλωσιν: Ὅρκον εἶπεν τὸν νόμον· ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ ὅρκος τίθησι
θεὸν ἐν ψυχῇ, οὕτω καὶ ὁ νόμος εἰσάγει θεὸν ἐν ψυχῇ· καὶ ὃν τρόπον πάλιν ἀναιρεῖ
ἡ ἐπιορκία θεὸν ἐκ ψυχῆς, οὕτω καὶ παρανομία ἐκβάλλει θεὸν ἀπ' αὐτῆς. ἐὰν οὖν,
φησίν, νόμου τεθέντος ἀκούσωσι καὶ μὴ ἐξαγορεύσωσιν ἑαυτῶν τὰς ἁμαρτίας,
φοβηθέντες καὶ αἰσχυνθέντες ἀνθρώπους, ὑποσκελισθήσονται. οὕτω δὴ καὶ ὁ ∆αυίδ·

Σολομὼν φησίν· Ὁ ἐπικαλύπτων ἀσέβειαν ἑαυτοῦ οὐκ εὐοδωθήσεται, ὁ δὲ
ἐξηγούμενος καὶ ἐλέγχων ἀγαπηθήσεται. καὶ ὁ ∆αυὶδ Εἶπα, φησίν, Ἐξαγορεύσω κατ'
ἐμοῦ τὴν ἀνομίαν μου τῷ κυρίῳ, καὶ σὺ ἀφῆκας τὴν ἀσέβειαν τῆς καρδίας μου. καὶ

english: Those having sheep and goats, that is, those possessing passions and impasses. Thus also he brought forward those having weeds and those having grain having grain, naming them according to the best and worst skill. Such is also what is said by Paul, 'Love does not fail' (1 Cor 13:8), instead of 'He who has love.' A righteous king raises up a land: Christ raises up the rational nature, but the antichrist undermines it. And to a poor man there is no discerning mind: surely he is poor who does not have a discerning mind.

And a foolish man being angry is laughed at and does not fall: 'And upon him, says David, they will laugh and say, Behold a man who did not set God as his helper' (Ps 35:16; Ps 36:14). Men of blood hate the holy, but the upright seek its soul: this one seeks the soul of a righteous man, he who wishes to understand things as they have been thought. A wise man is stored up by parts: this one stores up his passion by parts, namely, he who is angry at things toward the righteous, or he who consumes his passion by parts through long-suffering; and toward the simple one the former should be spoken, but toward the diligent the latter.

There shall not be an interpreter for the nations to the lawless: to those who have kept the law there shall be an interpreter; but to those who have acted lawlessly, an interpreter there shall not be, but a punisher shall be; if indeed not a word but a rod is given to the lawless for the nations. A hard servant will not be instructed by words: because no one is hard by nature, it demonstrates, 'For even if he should understand, he will not obey' (Exod 7:22); for he who is hard by nature would never understand anything right. I say this because of Pharaoh the hard...

Having been set upon Israel, and having been disciplined not by words but by beating. He who squanders shall be a servant from childhood. If squandering makes one sin, and everyone doing the sin is a slave to sin, then everyone who squanders is a slave to sin.

Pride humbles a man: Now he calls the wickedness of the rational soul 'pride'. He who divides with a thief hates his own soul: The thief, he says, does not come except to steal and to sacrifice and to destroy. If, after an oath is proposed, hearing them do not announce: He spoke an oath according to the law; for just as the oath sets God in the soul, so also the law introduces God into the soul; and in whatever way perjury again removes God from the soul, so also lawlessness casts God out of it. If, therefore, he says, having heard the law being set, they do not confess their sins, having feared and been ashamed of men, they shall be tripped up.

So also David: 'I have sworn and I have stood to keep the judgments of your righteousness' (Ps 119:76). And again Solomon says: 'He who covers his impiety shall not prosper, but he who explains and reproves shall be loved.' And David said, he says: 'I said, I will confess my lawlessness to the Lord, and you forgave the impiety of my heart' (Ps 32:5). And 'Say, you first, your lawlessness.'

Many heal the faces of leaders: In doing what is right we heal the angels; for they themselves are the leaders of us, having taken us from the beginning, when the Most High divided the nations and set the borders of the nations according to the number of his angels. λογικῆς ψυχῆς, καθ' ἣν τῶν ἀντικειμένων αὐτῇ κεκράτηκεν ἐχθρῶν. Ἡ τοιαύτη
σκύλων οὐκ ἀπορήσει: Νικήσαντες τὴν ἀντικειμένην δύναμιν σκυλεύομεν αὐτήν,
τοὺς περὶ αὐτῆς λόγους μανθάνοντες. Μηρυομένη ἔρια καὶ λίνον: Μηρύεται ἔρια καὶ
λίνον ψυχὴ τοὺς περὶ ἐμψύχων καὶ ἀψύχων λόγους 122 γυμνάζουσα, ἢ τοὺς περὶ
πρακτικῆς καὶ φυσικῆς ἐξετάζουσα λόγους. ἔλεγε δέ τις ὅτι μηρύεται ἔρια καὶ λίνον
ψυχὴ τὴν περὶ σωμάτων καὶ ἀσωμάτων θεωρίαν διὰ τῆς πρακτικῆς ἕλκουσα πρὸς
αὐτήν. Καὶ ἀνισταμένη ἐκ νυκτῶν (edd. ἀνίσταται ἐ. ν. καὶ) ἔδωκε βρώματα τῷ οἴκῳ:
Τὴν ἐκ νυκτὸς ἀνισταμένην ψυχὴν ἐγρηγορυῖαν εὑρίσκει ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἥλιος·
πάντως δὲ καὶ προσευχομένην ἵνα μὴ ἐμπέσῃ εἰς πειρασμόν· σπεύδει γὰρ καὶ αὐτὴ

26
english: The father has given to the son. What woman will find a brave one? Bravery is an excellent state of the rational soul, by which it has mastered the opposing forces of enemies. Such a thing will not be despoiled by dogs: having conquered the opposing power, we plunder it, learning the discourses concerning it.

Wool and linen being dyed: the soul is dyed like wool and linen, exercising itself in the discourses concerning the living and the non-living, or examining the discourses concerning the practical and the natural. And someone said that the soul is dyed like wool and linen, pulling the contemplation of bodies and incorporeal things toward it through the practical life.

And rising from the nights, she gave food to the household: the one who practices righteousness finds the soul rising from the night, being watchful; and certainly, also praying so that she might not fall into temptation; for she herself hastens to say, 'I awoke and became like a sparrow perching on a roof' (Ps 84:3). And her lamp is not extinguished through the whole night: a pure mind is a lamp, filled with spiritual contemplation. Her wicks are set in a lampstand: a pure mind is a lampstand, weaving virtue with virtue and doctrine with doctrine; or an articulated word, drawing spiritual contemplation from the mind.

Her husband does not care for those in the house when he lingers: the mind would not go forth, nor would it come to be in the contemplation of the incorporeal, without first correcting what is within; for the disturbance of the domestic affairs is accustomed to turn it back toward those from which it had departed; having acquired impassibility, it will linger in contemplation, and will not care for those in the house; for the passion is indeed [clothed in] practical and humble...
Wisdom, but desire [requires] temperance and self-control. Clothing itself of deep color and purple: The words of earth and sea are garments of the rational soul from the depths and the purple.

Another will say that the contemplation of events and the contemplation of the Holy Trinity are the clothing of a pure mind from the depths and the purple. He made linen cloths and gave them, but belts to the Canaanites (Mark 2:22): The linen cloth revealed on the roof (Mark 2:9) was a symbol of this sensible world; for the various animals contained therein showed the diverse characters of men, having been purified by the cross of Christ. If one linen cloth signified this world, perhaps many linen cloths contain the contemplation of various worlds, which the pure soul having contemplated, shared with others. If the Canaanites are interpreted as the lowly, it was not rightly that he gave the linen cloths to the lowly in mind, but rather the linen cloths to the pure, and to the Canaanites belts, which are symbols of practice, binding the passionate part of the soul.

Secure dwellings of its house: If the devil is king of all those in the waters and finds no rest through dry places, it is rightly said that the dwellings of the pure soul are secure. And he did not eat lazy grain: They say lazy grain is the grain of wickedness. For a prudent woman is blessed (Proverbs 31:30), but let this one praise the fear of the Lord (Psalm 111:10): If the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, the soul which happens to possess wisdom rightly praises the fear of the Lord, which has become to her a precursor of such knowledge.
They were collected from which we found them spread out. And again, these were corrected by the hands of Pamphilus and Eusebius.
